cands.name: Cecilia M. Aguiar-Curry
cands.bio: Democratic Assemblymember for District 4 since 2016 and Assembly Majority Leader since November 2023. Former Winters planning commissioner, city councilmember and the city's first woman mayor. Runs a water and land-use consulting business and co-owns a family walnut farm.

endorsements.text: Democratic Party of California, California Federation of Labor Unions (AFL-CIO), California Nurses Association and California Teachers Association, per Ballotpedia's 2026 list.
IUOE Local 3, National Union of Healthcare Workers, Equality California and YIMBY Action, per Ballotpedia's 2026 list.

cands.gaps: We found no documented position or action from her on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on investor or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, school vouchers or charters, or teacher pay raises. We could not read the list of bills she has sponsored, because the table on her Ballotpedia page was empty. We found no news coverage, so we cannot report on controversies, foreign ties or specific legislative actions. Her campaign statements about local housing measures, broadband and immigrants are her own claims and were not checked against bill records.

local.label: Roots 100: Ballotpedia says she was born in San Luis Obispo and grew up in western Yolo County, and she later returned to her hometown of Winters, where she held local office.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2016 and Majority Leader since November 2023. Earlier she was Winters planning commissioner, city councilmember and mayor (elected 2012). She also runs a water and land-use consulting firm and holds a business degree.
qual.why: Ten years of legislative service plus chamber leadership as Majority Leader, on top of local elected office and a consulting business in water and land use. Committee chairmanships were not counted.
qual.label: Ten years of legislative service plus chamber leadership as Majority Leader, on top of local elected office and a consulting business in water and land use. Committee chairmanships were not counted.

back-police-order.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she said she supports making sure law enforcement officers have the resources they need to do their jobs effectively. She also said she voted with the ACLU position on 12 of 13 police reform bills that year.

second-amendment.evidence: Her campaign site says she will push for sensible measures to curtail the epidemic of gun violence.

pro-life.evidence: In her 2022 Ballotpedia survey she said she strongly believes in a woman's right to control her own body. She said she joined the Legislative Women's Caucus in proposing legislation to strengthen and expand abortion access.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Her campaign site lists as a priority to fight climate change and protect California's farmland, air, water and open space.
